opening.headline: When you don't have time to read a lot of data and want to organize your sources, learn how to distinguish between Deep Research, which researches the outside world, and Gemini Notebook, which answers based on your own data.
body: There are dozens of theses, articles, and reports. It takes me a day just to read it, and once I'm done, I'm lost as to which sentence comes from which source. Moreover, having to research the outside world anew and reading the material I already have are all mixed together.

In this class, we will first look at the flow of Deep Research, which involves making a plan, exploring the web, and creating a report. Next, check Gemini Notebook, which provides answers with inline citations based on the sources you have entered, and how to add sources. Lastly, we will explain which tool is appropriate among reading 10 papers and external market research.
objectives: Can explain the role of Deep Research and Gemini Notebook
I can distinguish between external research and my own data-based work.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

screens.title: So much material to read, so little time.
screens.lead: Let's look at common problems that arise when data accumulates. When you select each item, an explanation will unfold.

items.prompt: Dozens of data are piled up
items.answer: Papers, articles, and reports are scattered across multiple folders and tabs. There is not enough time to read them all, and deciding the reading order is a burden.

items.prompt: After reading, the sources become scattered.
items.answer: It takes a day just to read, and later it becomes difficult to find which part of the material the sentences you organized came from. It is difficult to rewrite an organization without sources.

items.prompt: Two types of work are mixed
items.answer: Finding out about the size of a market you don't know about yet means researching the outside world, and drawing common conclusions from papers you've already downloaded means reading your own data. The two jobs require different tools.

items.prompt: So what questions do you need to ask?
items.answer: I first ask whether the material I want to organize is already in my hand or out there. If it's outside, it's Deep Research. If it's in my hands, it's Gemini Notebook.

screens.outro: First, let's think about what takes the longest to read and organize the material.

screens.title: Thinking: The most time-consuming step
screens.lead: Read the questions and think for yourself first. There is no need to submit an answer, and when you select an item, the instructor's thoughts unfold.

items.prompt: What steps take the most time to read and organize your material?
items.answer: It can be divided into three stages: finding data, reading, summarizing, and organizing sources. Each person has a different bottleneck, and the effectiveness of the tool varies depending on what stage the bottleneck is at.

items.prompt: Find, read, summarize, or organize sources?
items.answer: If searching takes the longest, Deep Research, which explores the outside world, is helpful. If reading and checking the evidence takes a long time, Gemini Notebook, which provides answers based on sources, is helpful.

items.prompt: What does it take to believe a summary?
items.answer: You should be able to identify which part of the material the summary comes from. Both functions have one thing in common: they show the source together, but they do it in a different way.

screens.outro: Now let's start with Deep Research, which investigates the outside world.

screens.title: Deep Research: Automating External Research
screens.lead: The following steps show the sequence in which Deep Research proceeds. Select the next arrow to follow step by step.

visual.alt: Deep Research flow chart with four steps: planning, search, inference, and reporting.
labels: Plan: Turn the prompt into a multi-item study plan.
Search: Web (default Google Search), select Gmail·Drive·Chat
Inference: Read what you gather and decide what to do next
Reporting: Multi-page report, Audio Overview, Canvas
My data: Upload files and add notebooks

steps.title: What is it?
steps.body: Deep Research is Gemini's agent-like feature. It browses many sites on the web on your behalf, including Gmail, Drive, and Chat if you choose, weighs what it finds, and creates a multi-page report. You can conduct in-depth, real-time research on almost any topic.

steps.title: 1) Planning
steps.body: First, we turn your prompts into a personalized, multi-item study plan. This is the step to decide what to investigate and in what order.

steps.title: 2) Search
steps.body: With a plan, you can self-search and explore the web to find relevant and up-to-date information. If selected, it will also find Gmail, Drive, and Chat. By default, Google Search is included as a source, and you can change the source or add other sources such as personal Gmail or Drive, upload files, or add notebooks.

steps.title: 3) Inference
steps.body: Read the information you have gathered over and over again and think about it before deciding on your next course of action. At this point, the thought process is shown to the user. Rather than simply concatenating search results, this is the step of deciding the next investigation based on what you found.

steps.title: 4) Reporting
steps.body: The results are generated in a more detailed and insightful multi-page report, completed in minutes. Reports can be listened to in Audio Overview and turned into interactive content or quizzes in Canvas.

steps.title: Terms of Use and Limits
steps.body: You must be 18 years or older and logged in to the Gemini app. There is a limit to the number of survey requests per day and the number of requests that can run simultaneously, and when you get close to the limit, you are notified of the number of requests remaining for the day. Google AI Pro and Ultra users can use higher limits and higher quality models.

screens.outro: Now that we've checked the external research, let's take a look at Gemini Notebook, which answers based on my own data.

screens.title: Gemini Notebook: Add sources and source-based answers
screens.lead: Select each tab to learn about the notebook's structure, sources, evidence-based answers, and output format.

visual.alt: Gemini Notebook screen mockup consisting of source panel, chat panel, and studio panel.

tabs.label: What is a notebook?
tabs.body: Gemini Notebook is an AI research assistant that helps you refine and organize your ideas. A notebook is a collection of source code for a project, and each notebook is independent so you don't access information from multiple notebooks at once. Previously named NotebookLM, the same independent product was renamed Gemini Notebook. Supports over 80 languages.

tabs.label: add source
tabs.body: Create a new notebook and add a source with Upload a source. Sources include PDFs, web URLs, public YouTube videos, audio files, pasted text, Google Docs, Slides (up to 100 pages), Sheets, Word, PowerPoint, CSV, Markdown, images, ePub, etc. The source is a copy or automatic synchronization of the imported or uploaded document, and the model answers based on the uploaded source. Each source can be up to 500,000 words or 200MB of uploaded file, and Free users can use up to 50 sources per notebook. Documents without rights will not be uploaded.

tabs.label: Source-based answer
tabs.body: The Chat panel shows a summary of all your sources and lets you ask questions or take actions on them. Answers to questions asked of the notebook are source-based and include inline citations for accuracy, transparency, and trustworthiness. If you only want to target specific sources, select them individually in the Source panel. It is different from a regular conversation in that you can check which word is in which document by directly clicking on it.

tabs.label: output format
tabs.body: In the Studio panel, convert your sources into formats such as notes, audio outlines, video outlines, mind maps, and reports. You can also create study guides and briefings, flashcards and quizzes, infographics, and slide decks. This reduces the reading burden by converting the source into an easy-to-understand format.

tabs.label: Gemini Apps and Management
tabs.body: Notebooks also appear in the Gemini app, so you can chat with them in Gemini, and if you rename them or add sources on one side, they'll sync to the other side. Conversations you have with a notebook in Gemini appear in the notebook's Sources panel in a read-only context when you select them. In your organization, Workspace administrators can turn Gemini Notebooks on or off on a per-user basis.

screens.outro: Now that we've confirmed the characteristics of the two tools, let's apply them to two tasks.

screens.title: Explanatory example: Reading 10 papers and conducting external market research
screens.lead: The instructor explains tool selection for both tasks. Select the next arrow to follow your decision.

steps.title: Reading two tasks
steps.body: Task A involves extracting common methods and conclusions from the 10 papers that have already been downloaded. Task B is to find out the size and competition status of the market that we are not yet familiar with. Both involve reading and organizing data, but the difference is where the data is located.

steps.title: Step 1: Do I have the materials in my hands?
steps.body: The 10 papers for Task A are already in my hands. In this case, there is no need to search again, so I put it as a source in Gemini Notebook. Create a new notebook and upload all thesis PDFs to Upload a source.

steps.title: Step 2: Check with quotes and ask questions
steps.body: In Chat, we ask, ‘What are the common methods and conclusions of the 10 pieces?’ The answer has an in-line citation, so you can click to check which sentence in which paper the conclusion came from. To compare only specific papers, select only those sources in the Source panel. If necessary, turn your organized results into a study guide or briefing.

steps.title: Step 3: Is the data out there?
steps.body: For task B, the materials are not in my hands and are out there. In this case, Deep Research is correct. Write down prompts about market size and competition, create a research plan, and explore the web to create a report.

steps.title: Step 4: Scope your sources and get the report
steps.body: The default source is Google Search. If necessary, I change the source or upload my own information so we can investigate together. When the report comes out, check the source directly for the numbers you need. You can also listen to the report in Audio Overview and skim it on the go.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: If my data is the focus, it's a notebook, and if outside research is the focus, it's deep research. The two tools can also be used sequentially. You can add notebooks to your Deep Research report, or place your findings as a source in a notebook to use as a basis for further questions.

screens.outro: Now that we've identified the criteria for tool selection, let's summarize the lesson.

screens.title: Summary: My data is notebook, external research is deep research.
screens.lead: Let's summarize what we've seen so far. Please read this while thinking about which side your work is closer to.

paragraphs: Deep Research automates out-of-the-box research with a flow of planning, searching the web, making inferences, and generating reports. The default source is Google Search, but you can also use Gmail, Drive, and Chat if you choose. There are limits on the number of daily and simultaneous requests.

Gemini Notebook provides answers with citations based on the sources you enter. A notebook is a collection of independent sources for a project, and adding sources is the starting point of work. You can also turn your sources into study guides, briefings, audio outlines, and mind maps.

The question that separates the two tools is where the data is. If my data is the focus, it's a notebook, and if outside research is the focus, it's deep research. Your notebook doesn't scan the entire Internet, and Deep Research doesn't always look at your mail.

Either way, you need to get into the habit of checking the basis for your results yourself. Notebook lets you click on inline citations to get that part of the source, while Deep Research checks the source of your report.

Also remember the criteria for selecting materials. I only upload materials I have the rights to as sources, and if the source changes, the answer on the notebook may also change. Deep Research has limits, so it is best not to use it for light checks. If you're just checking one short fact, general conversation or the source view function are sufficient. Conversely, if you have a deep question that requires synthesizing multiple sources, Deep Research is appropriate even if it takes time.
If my work requires both types, I can collect data through external research, organize it as a source in my notebook, and continue writing in the order of checking the evidence and asking questions.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: Each notebook is independent, so information from multiple notebooks is not automatically combined. Materials that you wish to cover together must be placed as sources in the same notebook.

glossary.def: Gemini's agent-like functionality allows you to create a research plan, research multiple sources, and create a multi-page report.
It is an AI research assistant that provides answers based on the sources you enter. Its previous name was NotebookLM.
Materials such as documents, URLs, and audio that you place on your notebook as imported or uploaded copies or automatically synchronized copies.
A citation that indicates the location of the source on which the answer is based.
This is an output format that summarizes a report or source using voice.

misconceptions.myth: Your notebook searches the entire Internet.
misconceptions.fact: Gemini Notebook's model answers are based on the sources I posted. Deep Research is in charge of investigating the outside world.

misconceptions.myth: Deep Research always looks at my mail.
misconceptions.fact: The default source is Google Search. Gmail, Drive, and Chat explore together only when you choose.

misconceptions.myth: Information is automatically merged between notebooks.
misconceptions.fact: Each notebook is independent, so information from multiple notebooks is not written at once.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Deep Research conducts external research through a flow of planning, search, inference, and reporting.
Gemini Notebook provides answers with citations based on the sources you provide.
Adding sources is the starting point for working with your notebook.
If my data is the focus, it's a notebook, and if outside research is the focus, it's deep research.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Do I already have the material I need to read and organize, or is it out there?

checks.q: Put the flow of deep research in the right order
items: Turn the prompt into a multi-item study plan
Browse the web and find Gmail, Drive, and Chat if necessary
Infer what you have collected and decide your next course of action
checks.explain: Make a plan, collect data, make inferences, decide the next action, and finally create a report.
checks.intro: Arrange the steps of Deep Research in order.
checks.correctFeedback: The order is correct. You got the order of planning, exploration, reasoning, and reporting right.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The order is out of order. A plan is made, data is collected, reasoning is made, next actions are decided, and a report is created at the end.

checks.q: While extracting common methods and conclusions from the 10 papers I have already downloaded, I also want to check which paper refers to which statement. Which one is best?
options: Investigate the entire outer web with Deep Research
Put it as source code in your notebook and receive the answer with inline citations.
Read papers aloud with Gemini Live
Summarizes as a general conversation without the Sources button
checks.explain: If I have the material in my hands, I put it as source material in my notebook. The model answers based on the uploaded source, and you can check the source with inline citations.

wrong.0: Deep Research is about investigating the outside world.
wrong.2: Live is a verbal conversation and is not intended to verify source evidence.
wrong.3: General conversation is not suitable for source-based citation verification.

checks.intro: This is a case where I would like to check the source in my thesis. Choose the right features.
checks.correctFeedback: That's right. Once you have the material in your hands, you can put it as a source in your notebook and use inline citations to check which paper it refers to.
checks.incorrectFeedback: External web research, audio features, and citation-free summaries do not fill this need. Look for features that meet both conditions: the material already exists and the source needs to be verified.
